intent.text: Revising my position in light of rec's point. The identity hook rewrites every Bash call, so removing the rule outright also reaches every session: ordinary allowed commands start prompting, measured in the README. Removal is not free for the non-identity sessions either. So I now agree with rec on the shape of the answer, and I'd add two things. (a) Do the three-form test first (bare export; export ';' destructive command; export + newline + command), plus a value containing a single quote, and the two-hook log check. This is cheap and should happen before anyone relies on the rule. (b) Scope matters more than the verdict. Whatever is kept should not sit in ~/.claude/settings.json, because global settings reload live into every session. Put it in a project-scoped settings file for the workspaces that run the identity hook, and check that other sessions' Bash behavior is unchanged afterwards. If (a) fails on any chained form, remove the rule and move identity off the Bash prefix, as rec suggests. Proposed resolution for Joseph: keep for now only as a project-scoped rule, test first, global rule removed once the project-scoped one is verified. I'd accept a 'keep with conditions' as the recorded outcome.
